whats.VCs will make billions on Anthropic’s IP: Shows how AI investment gains can flow more to big partners like Amazon than to early investors.
whats.QwikBuild raises $2.3M pre-seed to expan: Fresh funding for enterprise AI tools shows investors still see demand for workplace AI platforms.
whats.Workforce shake-up is here to stay. Brac: Signals that managers should plan for ongoing shifts in team structures, not a one time change.
whats.Preparing people to put AI to work: Highlights that training staff to use AI well is becoming as important as adopting the technology itself.
whats.Cognizant restructures software engineer: Shows a major IT firm reshaping its engineering teams as clients expect clearer value from AI spending.

term.def: A shared software system that lets different teams in a company use AI tools together, instead of each team buying separate apps.

prompt.prompt: List three roles in [your team] that AI could change in the next two years, and suggest one reskilling step for each.

quiz.q: TechCrunch reports that VCs will earn billions from Anthropic's IPO, but Amazon is set to earn far more.
quiz.why: This directly restates what TechCrunch's headline says about who profits most from the IPO.

quiz.q: Livemint reports that Cognizant is restructuring its software engineering business as clients seek AI returns.
quiz.why: This matches Livemint's headline about Cognizant's restructuring move.

quiz.q: AI can fully replace human judgment in every business decision.
quiz.why: AI can support decisions with data and patterns, but final judgment calls still need human context and accountability.

quiz.q: Reskilling current employees is often a practical way to adapt to AI changes, instead of always hiring new people.
quiz.why: Training existing staff on new tools usually costs less and keeps valuable experience inside the company.

quiz.q: Every company must build its own AI model from scratch to use AI well.
quiz.why: Most businesses use existing AI platforms or tools built by others rather than building models themselves.
